citation.title: Topology optimization of 2D structures with nonlinearities using deep learning
citation.authors: Diab W. Abueidda; Seid Koric; Nahil A. Sobh
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (2002.01896); article text matches the version of record

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The authors claim that trained CNNs can provide optimized designs for nonlinear and stress-constrained structures immediately, avoiding iterative optimization.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical-to-ML speed-up factor or paired inference time is reported.
claim.alternatives: Abstract also describes accurate prediction of designs; Section 5 reports image-similarity scores.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP-based nonlinear topology optimization; used to generate ground-truth designs
baseline.hardware_classical: iForge HPC: Intel Skylake nodes, 40 cores, 192 GB RAM; a personal computer with Core i5 vPro is also reported for single-task data generation
baseline.hardware_ml: NVIDIA V100 GPU, 32 GB; model inference also described on a laptop without specification
baseline.classical_time: A single task takes about 25 min on Core i5 vPro (linear) and about 90 min (nonlinear); Section 3
baseline.training_time: 1.25 h (linear) and 1.5 h (nonlinear) on V100; Section 5
baseline.data_generation_cost: 15,000 linear data pairs at 0.31 min/data point on HPC; 18,000 nonlinear data points at 3.2 min/data point; Section 3
baseline.quality_metric: Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), mean squared error, and selected image comparisons; Section 5
baseline.quality_gap: Mean test DSC reported as 0.964 for nonlinear and 0.984 for stress-constrained case; no compliance/objective gap reported; Section 5

R1.evidence: Abstract and Section 6 claim negligible inference/instant predictions; reported comparisons use DSC/image agreement and do not establish matched compliance or equal time/FE budget.

R2.evidence: Sections 2–3 describe a commercial Abaqus optimization pipeline and provide no comparison of its solver efficiency with a strong baseline.

R3.evidence: Sections 3 and 5 report dataset-generation rates and model training times, but no break-even use count or explicit per-query-only scope.

R4.evidence: Section 5 evaluates predictions mainly using DSC/MSE and selected design images; returned designs are not reported as FE-verified for performance and failed designs are not counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: 15,000 linear and 18,000 nonlinear data points are reported as generated; 10% test split for each model (Sections 3 and 5)

notes: Dataset cases are generated with the classical optimizer, but the article does not compare matched classical and ML runtimes.
